landing.tagline: The shared notebook of your campaign
landing.intro: Ex Libris is where a tabletop RPG group writes its campaign together: places, characters, events and secrets, each one seen only by the players who should know it.

rooms.title: Rooms and roles
rooms.text: One Room per campaign. The Master runs it, Players join with a link, and each role holds only inside its Room.

documents.title: Documents and Notes
documents.text: Places, characters, events, objects: write them as Documents, add Notes, and link them with mentions that work both ways.

visibility.title: Visibility and Reveal
visibility.text: Hide anything from anyone. The Master always sees everything, Players see what is shown to them, and a Reveal opens it up when the story calls for it.

comments.title: Comments and threads
comments.text: Discuss every Document in a thread of Comments and replies, with reactions, pins and posts in character.

maps.title: Maps
maps.text: Draw relationship maps between Documents or pin places on a geographic map, and edit them together.

export.title: Export
export.text: Take the campaign with you: a PDF manual in three styles, or JSON and Markdown for your own tools.

sections.title: Sections and the Room home
sections.text: Build your Room's landing page with Sections: Documents by Tag, maps, Session 0 and Clocks.

session.title: Session 0
session.text: Agree how to play: Lines and Veils, Stars and Wishes, questions and polls.

clocks.title: Clocks
clocks.text: Track what is coming with segmented clocks, as a race or in turns.

steps.create: Create a Room for your campaign.
steps.invite: Invite your players with a link.
steps.write: Write the campaign together, each of you seeing what you should.

roomLanding.title: The Room's home
roomLanding.body: Every Room opens on its own landing page: cards for the Documents, the maps, Session 0 and Clocks, and the Sections the Master has built.

sections.title: Sections
sections.body: Each card is a Section the Master put together. Click one to open its page.

sectionPage.title: Inside a Section
sectionPage.body: A Section holds blocks: Documents picked by Tag, maps, Session 0 steps, Clocks. The Master arranges them in edit mode.

roomIndex.title: The Room Index
roomIndex.body: This tab opens the Room's index: every Tag and every map, one click away from any page.

documentCard.title: Documents
documentCard.body: Each card is a Document: a character, a place, an object. The badge says who can see it.

document.title: A Document's page
document.body: Name, subtitle and description, with images and Owners beside them. Owners can edit it, and so can the Master.

documentText.title: Notes and mentions
documentText.body: Notes add paragraphs under the description. The text supports Markdown, and a #mention links another Document: the link works both ways.

mentionMap.title: The mention map
mentionMap.body: Mentions draw a live map of how Documents are tied together. It follows what you write.

comments.title: Comments and replies
comments.body: Every Document has its thread: replies, reactions, posts in character, and Comments only some members see.

visibility.title: Visibility and Reveal
visibility.body: This Document is for the Master only. Every Document, Note and Comment has its own visibility, and the Master reveals it from the ⋮ menu when the story calls for it.

viewAs.title: See what the Players see
viewAs.body: Switch to Marco or Giulia: what they cannot see disappears. The Master can preview the Room as any member in the same way.

search.title: Search
search.body: Search every Document, Note and Comment you can see. Ctrl K opens it from anywhere in the Room.

freeMap.title: Free boards
freeMap.body: Document cards and arrows on a free board, to follow who wants what. Arrows between the same two cards bend apart. The Master can let Players draw on it too.

splitView.title: Side-by-side preview
splitView.body: The Preview button splits the screen: click any card and its Document opens on the right, so you can read while you plan.

linkNote.title: Relational links
linkNote.body: A Note flagged as a Relational link turns its mentions into ties: they feed the mention map and the Documents' backlinks.

geoMap.title: Geographic maps
geoMap.body: Pin places on a map image and outline regions; each place leads to its Document. Links between places can curve.

sessionZero.title: Session 0
sessionZero.body: Before the first session the table agrees how to play: Lines and Veils, Stars and Wishes, questions, polls. Here it has already been played.

poll.title: Polls
poll.body: The Master asks, everyone votes. Settings decide who sees the names and when the tally shows. This one chose where the story begins.

clocks.title: Clocks
clocks.body: Segmented clocks track what is coming: an escape, a plan, the dawn. Groups run them as a race or in turns.

versions.title: Version history
versions.body: Owners and the Master can read every earlier version of a Document, Notes included, and restore one.

alsoThere.title: And there is more
alsoThere.body: With an account you can also export a PDF manual in three styles, import and export JSON and Markdown, generate mentions, read aloud, search images for maps and add friends. They write data, so the demo only mentions them.

playerDocuments.title: Now as a Player
playerDocuments.body: You are Marco, who plays Jun. The Master-only Documents are gone, and his private one, the Net Café, appears for him alone.

playerDocument.title: A Player's own Document
playerDocument.body: This Document is private: only Marco and the Master can see it. Giulia's view of the Room does not even list it.

playerMap.title: A Player's map
playerMap.body: The Master's hidden card and its arrows are missing. Switch back to Master in the banner when you are done.

end.title: That's Ex Libris
end.body: Sign in to create your own Room, or keep exploring the demo.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains which personal data this app processes, why, where it is kept and how you can exercise your rights under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.body: The data controller is {{name}}. For any question about your data, or to exercise your rights, write to {{email}}.

data.title: What data we process
data.body:
Only what the app needs to work:

- Sign-in data from the provider you choose (Google, Discord or GitHub): an account identifier, your email address, and your name and picture, which are copied once as the default name and avatar of your profile.
- Your profile: display name, pronouns, description and avatar, which you can change or remove at any time on the Account page.
- What you write and upload in Rooms: Documents, Notes, Comments, reactions, images and PDF attachments, with who created them and when.
- Your Friends, friend requests and friend code, and the Room invitations you send or receive.
- Usage and technical data: when you last opened each Document, the change history of Documents, each Room's log of role and visibility changes, and the request data servers record to deliver and protect the service (such as IP address, browser and time).

purposes.title: Why, and on what legal basis
purposes.body:
Your data is used only to provide the app to you and to the members of your Rooms (performance of a contract, art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and to keep it secure and working (legitimate interest, art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

It is not sold, it is not used for advertising or profiling, and the app uses no analytics or tracking tools. Your email is never shown to other users.

processors.title: Who processes it, and where
processors.body:
The app relies on these providers, which process data on our behalf:

- Supabase: database, file storage and sign-in, hosted in the European Union (Frankfurt, Germany).
- OVHcloud: the server that runs the app's backend, in the United Kingdom, which the European Commission recognises as offering adequate protection.
- Vercel: delivery of the web app's pages. Its network may serve requests from outside the European Union; transfers to the United States rely on the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses.
- Google, Discord and GitHub: only for the sign-in you choose, under their own privacy policies.
- Openverse, a WordPress.org project: when you search free images for a Document, the search is sent by our server, and the previews are loaded by your browser directly from Openverse, which therefore sees your IP address.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body:
- Your account and profile are kept until you delete your account.
- When you delete your account, your profile, avatar, Friends, reactions, Session 0 post-its and sign-in account are erased at once. Rooms where you were the only member are deleted with everything in them. In Rooms shared with others, what you wrote stays as part of the campaign, shown as written by an unknown user.
- A Room you delete is erased with everything in it.
- Room PDFs are deleted 24 hours after they are generated, and Document imports 7 days after they finish.
- Server logs are kept only as long as needed for operation and security, and are overwritten on a rolling basis.
- Backups kept by our providers are overwritten within their backup cycle.

rights.title: Your rights

storage.title: Cookies and local storage
storage.body: The app uses no cookies. It keeps a few items in your browser's storage that it needs to work: your sign-in session, the language you chose, your read-aloud voice and speed, the character you last posted as in each Room, the Room PDF notices you dismissed, and an invitation link you opened before signing in. They stay on your device: the session is removed when you sign out, the rest when you clear your browser's data.

edit.noGroups: No groups: all the Documents are together.
edit.groupHint: Pick one or more Tags: several Tags make a combination.
edit.deleteToolBody: Its votes, post-its and answers are deleted too. This can't be undone.

tool.draftHint: The players don't see it yet

clocks.title: Clocks
clocks.description: The Room's clocks: those in play, those in the background and those already closed.
clocks.signInRequired: Sign in to see this Room's clocks.
clocks.deleteBody: “{{name}}” and its history will be deleted. This can't be undone.

markPolicy.master_and_creator: The Master and whoever opened it

dialog.nameHint: Name it after the obstacle or the event, not the method.
dialog.sizeHint: From 2 to 16, odd ones too: 4, 6, 8 and 12 are just shortcuts.
dialog.labelsHintMaster: Type a new name to create one: the Room keeps it for later clocks.
dialog.closingConditionHint: Seen by everyone; the app doesn't check it.
dialog.stagesHint: Optional, like the stages of a countdown.
dialog.forwardOnlyHint: This clock's marks are never emptied.

noReturn.name: No going back
noReturn.detail: Players propose, no mark is emptied

rules.title: Clock rules
rules.presetsHint: They fill the three rules below; labels and mark kinds stay as they are.
rules.undoNoHint: Marks are never erased, not even by the Master; only the undo of a mistaken click stays.
rules.labelsHint: The Room's free labels, each with a colour; a clock carries up to 6.
rules.markKindsHint: Up to 6, optional: what a mark is made of in this game and who may use it.
rules.noTemplates: No templates: save one from a clock's dialog.

groups.name: Group name

modeHint.free: The clocks just sit together: the layers of a place, the factions.
modeHint.race: The first to close wins; if another closes before you confirm, it is a tie.
modeHint.turn: Some clocks are decisive: when one closes the turning point ends and the others lapse.
modeHint.sequence: They close in order: only the first open one takes marks, the others wait.

groups.clocksHint: In the order you pick them, up to {{max}}; a clock of another group moves here.
groups.decisiveHint: Write the outcome of the decisive clocks; leave the others empty.
groups.deleteBody: “{{name}}” goes away; its clocks stay, outside any group.
groups.empty: No clocks: edit the group to add some.
groups.raceTie: {{names}} closed: it is a tie, both happen.
groups.turnEnds: The turning point ends: {{labels}}. The other open clocks lapse.
groups.reveal: “{{name}}” is next, but the Players can’t see it. Reveal it?
